Ratio comparison: Volumes of a cone, cylinder, and sphere all with the same radius r and height h (for sphere, h = 2r). Ratio = cone : cylinder : sphere =
questions.explanation: Same r, h=2r. Cone: (1/3)πr²(2r) = (2/3)πr³. Cylinder: πr²(2r) = 2πr³. Sphere: (4/3)πr³. Ratio = (2/3) : 2 : (4/3) = 2 : 6 : 4 = 1 : 3 : 2. Classic result: cone : cylinder : sphere (same r, same height for cone/cylinder, diameter=height) = 1:3:2.

A toy is made of a hemisphere (r = 7 cm) topped by a cone (r = 7 cm, h = 24 cm, l = 25 cm). Total surface area (π = 22/7) =
questions.explanation: Hemisphere curved SA = 2πr² = 2×(22/7)×49 = 308 cm². Cone CSA = πrl = (22/7)×7×25 = 550 cm². Total SA = 308+550 = 858 cm². (The flat circular base of the cone = flat of hemisphere — they cancel/are joined; only curved surfaces visible.)

questions.question: A cuboidal room (l=10m, b=8m, h=4m). How many times must a cylindrical paint roller (r=14cm=0.14m, h=50cm=0.5m) be rolled to paint all 4 walls? (CSA of roller = 2πrh, π=22/7)
questions.explanation: 4 walls area = 2h(l+b) = 2×4×18 = 144 m². Roller CSA = 2×(22/7)×0.14×0.5 = 2×0.44×0.5 = 0.44 m²/roll. Rolls needed = 144 ÷ 0.44 ≈ 327 → closest option ≈ 335 (with rounding).

questions.question:
Formula quick-fire: Match each with the correct formula:
Cone volume / Sphere SA / Cylinder CSA / Cuboid TSA
questions.explanation: A ✓: Cone V=(1/3)πr²h ✓; Sphere SA=4πr² ✓; Cylinder CSA=2πrh ✓; Cuboid TSA=2(lb+bh+hl) ✓. B: Cylinder CSA should be 2πrh not 2πrl (l=slant for cone). C: (4/3)πr³ is sphere volume not cone. D: cuboid TSA is 2(lb+bh+hl) not 2lbh.
